thread:
mika: Heads up — after the merge of PR #1893 the runtime perf CI shows a sharp p95 jump (~35%). Seen it on canary and local reproduce on r1.10 images.

evan: I can reproduce. Kernel selector is hitting the fallback path much more often. Profiling attached below.

sarah: ugh. Did we change the seqlen heuristics in that PR or the kernel mapping table?

evan: both — heuristics tweak + small kernel routing change. The routing table now prefers packed kernels for seqlen < 128. For some workloads that increased kernel churn.

mika: ok let's bisect quickly. @andre can you start a git bisect on r1.10 against the perf job hash?

andre: starting git bisect now. starting point: release/1.10, good: 6a1f2c4 (before PR 1893), bad: HEAD (includes PR 1893). Running perf smoke scripts.

ci-bot: perf-job/eng-runtime#perf-171 started for commit 9c3f7a2 (PR 1893) — link: https://ci.redwood/perf/171

evan: early bisect result points to commit 9c3f7a2 -> kernel routing tweak. Repro script shows fallback_count increased from ~120/s to ~430/s for our tiny-chat workload.

sarah: can we try reverting only the routing table change (leave heuristics) to confirm?

mika: yes. Create a hotfix branch off release/1.10 and cherry-pick the revert for the routing change.

andre: cherry-picked revert commit 4f8b2d1 onto release/1.10-hotfix. Pushed branch: release/1.10-hotfix/kernel-routing-revert.

evan: running perf job against hotfix branch now. Command I ran locally:
```
git checkout release/1.10-hotfix/kernel-routing-revert
./scripts/perf/run_perf.sh --workload tiny-chat --runs 10
```

sarah: any numbers yet?

evan: initial run looks promising — p95 back down ~7% vs bad, fallback_count back near baseline. Need CI to confirm across matrices.

ci-bot: perf-job/eng-runtime#perf-172 queued for branch release/1.10-hotfix/kernel-routing-revert

mika: if CI confirms, plan: merge hotfix to release/1.10, tag patch, and then cherry-pick into main with a note. Also prepare release notes and rollout gating.

andre: preparing backport PR -> #1910. Includes unit test addition for kernel routing edge case and a short changelog.

sarah: QA — once CI green, I'll run the nightly mixed-load tests and spot check internal gating thresholds.

evan: small ask: add a perf-regression alert to the run so we get immediate slack pings if it slips during rollout. e.g., p95 delta > 10% trigger.

mika: good. Also add an automated verify step on the rollout convo: after canary pass (2 pods @ 10% traffic) validate p95 and fallback_count before 50% step.

deploy-bot: rollout started for release/1.10-hotfix/kernel-routing-revert -> canary: 2 pods, 10% traffic.

deploy-bot: canary passed health checks. Waiting for manual verify: @sarah

sarah: verified canary metrics (p50/p95/fallback_count). OK to proceed to 50%.

deploy-bot: rollout to 50% in progress.

deploy-bot: rollout complete to 100%.

mika: hotfix merged and tagged as v1.10.1. Thanks everyone. Follow-up: retro on why the heuristics change interacted poorly with kernel mapping; evan/sarah to own a short postmortem.

andre: PR #1910 merged, backported change cherry-picked to main as 2a9b3c7.

mika: closing thread — reopen if CI regression alerts spike. :thumbsup:
__notes: This document is a simulated eng-runtime slack thread capturing a bisect, cherry-pick revert, hotfix branch workflow and staged rollout. Messages are in chronological order and include bots and short commands as per Slack style.
